s: a 19th-century-inspired café lit only by candles and paraffin lamps
w: A Gamla Stan café built entirely around an 1800s mood -- no music, no electric lighting, just candles and paraffin lamps over husmanskost, wine, beer, coffee and cake. New enough to still feel like a discovery, but styled to seem like it's been on Stora Nygatan far longer than it has -- a genuine hidden-gem counterpoint to the old town's main tourist run.
_facts: Located at Stora Nygatan 31, 111 27 Stockholm, Gamla Stan
Styled as a 19th-century-inspired café: candlelight and paraffin lamps only, no music
Serves Swedish home cooking (husmanskost) alongside coffee, cake, wine and beer

s: a 1960s basement market hall of 40-plus global food stalls under Hötorget
w: A market hall built in the 1960s beneath Hötorget square -- itself a trading site since the 17th century -- packing more than 40 vendors under one roof: Swedish fishmongers and cheesemongers alongside Turkish, Italian, Finnish, South American and East Asian stalls. Unglamorous fluorescent-lit basement energy rather than a design showpiece, and busy with locals rather than coach parties.
_facts: Located beneath Hötorget square, 111 57 Stockholm, Norrmalm
Market hall built in the 1960s; Hötorget has been a trading site since the 17th century
Home to more than 40 vendors, mixing Swedish produce stalls with Turkish, Italian, Asian and South American food shops

s: an organic garden and café built on a former dynamite factory site
w: A volunteer-run organic show garden and café a few metro stops from the centre, in a green cove that was once the site of Alfred Nobel's dynamite factory. Homemade cakes and coffee served among the beds and greenhouses -- a slow, restorative pause that trades city noise for birdsong within twenty minutes of downtown.
_facts: Located at Vinterviksvägen 30, 117 65 Stockholm, Hägersten-Liljeholmen, near Aspudden metro station
Site of a former Nobel-associated dynamite/explosives factory (Vinterviken), now a public park and organic demonstration garden
Run in part by volunteers as a garden association (trädgårdsförening) with an attached café
Café serves homemade baking, coffee and light food; open seasonally
